title: `modulus` on doubles
description: DuckDB's `%` on doubles is `fmod` (native): `7.5 % 2 = 1.5`, `% 0.0` is NaN, or an error with `error_on_division_by_zero`. sverify raises on a zero divisor and writes out the NaN and infinite cases, so only finite operands reach `%`.
Changed (#257): an infinite dividend with a non-NaN divisor now raises a domain error instead of giving NaN, since no operation creates a NaN.
Polars' `%` floors (the sign of the divisor); numpy's `fmod` covers it.
reference: Substrait: `functions_arithmetic.yaml` has no `fp32`/`fp64` impl of `modulus`. DataFusion writes `modulus` with `fp64` arguments anyway.

Lean: `"modulus"` always parsed to integer `imod` ([`Parse.lean:956`](../../frontend/Sverify/Frontend/Parse.lean#L956)); `mkFloatCall` ([`Parse.lean:1032`](../../frontend/Sverify/Frontend/Parse.lean#L1032)) had no case for it. On doubles, `imod` worked on the float codes: `7.5 % 2.0` evaluated to a 300-digit integer, `d % 0.0` to NULL. A deviation, and a soundness bug, since the plan was accepted and the result was wrong.

Fixed (#203): a `modulus` of doubles is C's `fmod` (`FloatCode.fmod` in [`Float.lean`](../../core/Sverify/Core/Float.lean)), as DuckDB, DataFusion and Spark compute `%`: the sign of the dividend (`-7.5 % 2.0 = -1.5`); NaN for a NaN or an infinite dividend; the dividend for an infinite divisor. It is exact, computed on the codes. A zero divisor is an error, as on integers and as #185 decides for an omitted `on_division_by_zero`, so `verify` can prove it absent. Substrait has no such impl; the reference takes the plan DataFusion writes as `fmod`.
Since #256 it is sverify's own function `sverify_fmod`, which Lean writes and the frontends emit; Lean still reads DataFusion's `modulus` of doubles as the same function.

provenance.notes: Compute modulus of doubles as C fmod; a zero divisor raises (commit 8e400f6).
`sverify_fmod`; an infinite dividend raises a domain error.
NaN for a zero divisor or an infinite dividend (duckdb-R15-double-modulus).

evidence.note: BindBinaryFloatingPoint: NaN from std::fmod with ieee_floating_point_ops, else BinaryZeroCheckWrapper raises or gives NULL
BinaryZeroCheckWrapper: a zero divisor raises `Division by zero` or sets NULL by error_on_division_by_zero

provenance.notes: FLOAT `%` by zero is NaN under `ieee_floating_point_ops` (the default), as DOUBLE's is.

evidence.note: for FLOAT and DOUBLE, `val % 0` → nan for 1, -1, 0, nan and inf
with ieee_floating_point_ops = false `val % 0` raises `Division by zero`
and with error_on_division_by_zero = false too it gives NULL

provenance.notes: The test loops over FLOAT and DOUBLE, so it settles `on_division_by_zero` of `%` at fp32.
